question: Why Tibbett Allen left the Board in 1888 is unknown. He was elected for Jefferson District in 1887; the county court issued a rule against him on 3 September 1888 to show cause why he should not be removed for non-residence; he resigned and Frank Hume was appointed in his place on 2 October. The court never ruled, so there is no finding that he was non-resident, and nothing records where he lived. He was the last Black member until 1986. The Black press did not cover it: the Washington Bee carries nothing in any issue from August to December 1888, the Richmond Planet has one digitized issue in all of 1888 and it is silent, the People's Advocate had ceased by 1884, and the National Republican's digitized run ends in May 1888.
settles: The Alexandria County court order book for 1888 at the Library of Virginia, which would carry the rule and its disposition, and the Board's minute books at the Center for Local History, which the 1967 compilation (arlhist1967officials) was read from; neither is online. A residence for Allen in the 1880 census would settle where he lived.

Chichester's politics and the date he took the bench have not been established.
